limitations: The sharp constant applies to the two-block subclass, while the unrestricted fixed-fraction result identifies only the square-root order. The code-rate bound is sufficient rather than optimal, and equivalent formulations in older coding, orthogonal-array, or stopping literature remain a residual originality risk.
scientific_summary: In a two-iid-block Rademacher sequence, any stop in the second block has expected bias bounded sharply by the ordinary simple-walk maximum. Binary systematic-code constructions attain the endpoint while preserving k-wise independence for k linear in the full horizon, implying square-root worst-case bounded-stopping bias for every fixed independence fraction below one half.
